# Phase 2 baselines (generated by experiments/run_baselines.py)

1539 perturbations (1397 genes, 142 drugs), 22 symptoms, relation induces. Grouped split: 5-fold cross-validation with leakage groups by disease_cluster_and_targets (954 groups); out-of-fold predictions pooled. Unobserved pairs count as negatives (positive-unlabelled convention). Label selection data/processed/label_selection/better_v1_full_v2.parquet: 2228 of 4439 positive pairs set aside, neither positive nor negative in fitting or scoring (positive counts in the hold-out tables include them). Pooled metrics are computed on the pooled out-of-fold predictions; per-fold values are the mean and standard deviation over folds of the macro metric, which is immune to the base-rate artifact that pulls pooled AUROC of a constant-per-fold predictor below 0.5.

## Pathway-wise split, curated modules (each module of design section 3.2 held out in turn)

Per-symptom AUPRC inside one held-out module is not meaningful (sets of 4 to 8 genes with homogeneous symptom profiles), so only pooled per-symptom metrics and per-hold-out ranking metrics are shown.
 Raw pooled scores across hold-outs with different base rates carry the artifact of section 6.2 (review v0.4, finding 1); the rank-within-hold-out columns replace each score by its tie-averaged rank over (n + 1) inside its hold-out before pooling, and the stratified AUROC forms positive-negative pairs inside hold-outs only. The pathway-wise endpoint is defined on the rank-within-hold-out macro AUPRC.

Held out (perturbations, positive pairs): catecholamine (20, 155); serotonin_melatonin (12, 108); tetrahydrobiopterin (5, 15); gaba_glutamate (6, 40); urea_cycle (8, 26); heme_porphyrin (4, 20); sterol_lysosomal_lipid (9, 33); creatine_energy (6, 18); acetylcholine_histamine_adenosine (6, 42).

## Pathway-wise split, Human-GEM subsystems (every gene whose primary subsystem is the held-out one)

Subsystems are the reconstruction's own pathway partition; they cover many more annotated genes than the curated modules and are the candidate definition of the pre-registered pathway-wise split.
 Raw pooled scores across hold-outs with different base rates carry the artifact of section 6.2 (review v0.4, finding 1); the rank-within-hold-out columns replace each score by its tie-averaged rank over (n + 1) inside its hold-out before pooling, and the stratified AUROC forms positive-negative pairs inside hold-outs only. The pathway-wise endpoint is defined on the rank-within-hold-out macro AUPRC.

Held out (perturbations, positive pairs): Alanine, aspartate and glutamate metabolism (8, 28); Aminoacyl-tRNA biosynthesis (7, 12); Arginine and proline metabolism (11, 26); Bile acid biosynthesis (5, 15); Biopterin metabolism (6, 16); Cholesterol metabolism (5, 12); Curated neurotransmission (38, 226); Cysteine and methionine metabolism (8, 26); Glycerophospholipid metabolism (10, 45); Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism (5, 12); Glycosylphosphatidylinositol (GPI)-anchor biosynthesis (10, 15); Inositol phosphate metabolism (16, 47); Keratan sulfate degradation (6, 14); Leukotriene metabolism (6, 13); Lysine metabolism (14, 40); Metabolism of other amino acids (3, 12); N-glycan metabolism (11, 23); Nucleotide metabolism (22, 67); Omega-3 fatty acid metabolism (3, 10); Oxidative phosphorylation (19, 39); Pantothenate and CoA metabolism (3, 12); Phenylalanine, tyrosine and tryptophan biosynthesis (15, 112); Porphyrin metabolism (8, 26); Purine metabolism (10, 27); Sphingolipid metabolism (12, 26); Sulfur metabolism (3, 10); Tricarboxylic acid cycle and glyoxylate/dicarboxylate metabolism (5, 17); Valine, leucine, and isoleucine metabolism (4, 19).
